title: Unit factories, reconstructors and payload blocks cannot be configured: the panel is empty or lists unrelated items

path.to: Live client, campaign or custom game: place a ground-factory / additive-reconstructor / constructor / payload-router / payload-source (sandbox) and left-tap it with no block selected.

java: Java: place a ground-factory, tap it -> the panel lists its unit plans (dagger/crawler/nova); picking a plan calls configure(index) which sets UnitFactoryBuild.currentPlan (UnitFactory.java:59-75, 285-320).
Java: tap an additive-reconstructor -> the panel lists the unit command icons and applies configure(command) (Reconstructor.java:215-233).

Java: tap a constructor -> the panel lists producible payload blocks (Constructor.java:67-70); payload-router/payload-source list blocks+units (PayloadRouter.java:183-190, PayloadSource.java:113-117).
godot: Godot: place a ground-factory and tap it -> the panel shows a button for every item in the game (config_spec builds item options because def.has_items is true, desktop.rs:1376-1387) and pressing one does nothing: UnitFactoryBehavior has no configured() override (client/rust/mind-core/src/world/blocks/units/behavior.rs:114-189; trait default is a no-op at behavior/mod.rs:230).
Tap an additive-reconstructor or payload-source -> the panel renders only the clear row and X (no declared kinds and no has_items/has_liquids, desktop.rs:1372-1411), so no unit/block can be chosen.
Tap a constructor or payload-router -> the panel lists items, but the behaviors only accept ConfigValue::Block/Unit (constructor.rs:122-147; payload_router.rs:266), so each submitted item is dropped.
compare: Java renders each block's real unit/block picker and applies the selection; the port renders an item list (or an empty panel) and the submit is a no-op, so factory plans, reconstructor commands and payload recipes can never be chosen.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: MindInput.config_spec (client/rust/mind-gdext/src/input/desktop.rs:1360) only emits Item/Liquid options and only marks BlockKind::LogicBlock as text; the unit/block choice needs per-behavior ConfigKind declarations, their configured() handlers, and a fragment submit kind that carries the option kind.
plan.approach: 1) Declare accepted kinds per behavior (config_kinds): UnitFactory -> Number (Java sends the plan index), Constructor/PayloadRouter/PayloadSource -> Block/Unit (their configured() already handles those, constructor.rs:122 and payload_source.rs:135). 2) In config_spec, when a block declares Block/Unit (or its kind is Constructor/PayloadSource/PayloadRouter), add option rows that carry both the content name and its kind; the name already resolves to a typed Block/Unit through resolve_config (runtime.rs:214-221). 3) Emit the option kind through block_config_fragment.gd so the button submits 'content' with the right name (the fragment's _submit path already maps 'content' to ConfigValue::String -> typed content). 4) Implement configured() for UnitFactoryBehavior: write UnitFactoryBuild.current_plan with bounds clamp and reset progress when it changes (mirror UnitFactory.java:59-75); a factory's command row can follow once RTS unit commands land. 5) Keep the item/liquid fallback for undeclared blocks. 6) Narrow check: cargo test -p mind-core world::blocks::units plus an in-engine tap on a ground-factory that selects crawler and asserts current_plan == 1 via SimHost state JSON.
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-core world::blocks::units and an in-engine ground-factory tap that changes UnitFactoryBuild.current_plan (state JSON).

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (hud-world-ui): S2 high confidence - the unit/production side of the game is unconfigurable, so a factory can only ever build its default plan and a reconstructor cannot be given a command; payload rout/source selection (Erekir) is equally unreachable. This is the per-block-config half of BlockConfigFragment; the item/liquid pickers for sorters/unloaders/duct-routers do work. Distinct from the logic-scan switch/message items. In-engine verification pending.

title: Message and illuminator blocks open an empty config panel: message text and light colour cannot be edited

path.to: Live client: place a message block (custom game / editor map) or an illuminator and left-tap it.

java: Java: tap a message block -> a pencil button opens the @editmessage TextArea dialog; OK calls configure(text) (MessageBlock.java:109-140).
Java: tap an illuminator -> a pencil opens the colour picker; OK calls configure(rgba int) (LightBlock.java:109-133).
godot: Godot: tap a message block -> config_spec sets text:true only for BlockKind::LogicBlock (desktop.rs:1400) and the block has no items/liquids, so the fragment takes the options branch and renders only the clear row + X (block_config_fragment.gd:58-100); there is no pencil and no editor.

Even if the field appeared, a 'string' submit is lowered to ConfigValue::String (input/mod.rs:884) and then to SimValue::Content(value) (command_emit.rs:254), so resolve_config rejects arbitrary text as an unknown content name (sim/runtime.rs:214-231); MessageBehavior::configured already accepts ConfigValue::String (logic/blocks/message.rs:56-70).
Tap an illuminator -> the same empty panel and no behavior stores a colour: default_behavior has no LightBlock arm (behavior/mod.rs:498-605).
compare: Java opens a text/colour editor and stores the value; the port shows an empty panel and has no wire channel that can carry arbitrary text or a colour.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: config_spec's text flag (desktop.rs:1400) and the string config wire path (input/mod.rs:884 -> command_emit.rs:248 -> sim/runtime.rs:203): kind 'string' must stop being encoded as a content name.
plan.approach: 1) Emit text:true (or a 'message' kind) from config_spec for BlockKind::MessageBlock; the fragment's existing LineEdit then submits 'string' (block_config_fragment.gd:64-74). 2) Give the fixed-step config command a real text channel: add a ConfigValue/String variant to determinism::ConfigValue (or send Bytes) and map WorldConfigValue::String to it in to_sim_config, so resolve_config passes the raw string through instead of looking it up as content; keep name->content resolution for item/liquid/block options. 3) For the illuminator, add a LightBlock behavior storing the packed rgba int with a Number/Int configured() and a colour-picker control in the fragment (Java LightBlock.java:109-133). 4) Narrow check: cargo test -p mind-core sim with a Configure('set x 1' / message text) landing in the block state, plus in-engine: message block tap -> type -> OK -> state JSON shows the text.
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-core sim (msg string configure round-trip) and an in-engine message-block text edit reflected in SimHost state JSON.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (hud-world-ui): S3 high confidence - message blocks (a staple of Erekir/editor maps) and illuminators can never be edited, so their content is stuck at the default. The string->Content encoding is shared with the logic-editor gap recorded as 'No in-game logic editor: processor code cannot be viewed or edited...' (logic code-scan item); this record covers the different block family and the missing text flag. In-engine verification pending.

title: Selecting a block shows no info panel: no name, hotkey, requirement/cost rows or '?' content button

path.to: Live client, any game mode: select a block in the bottom-right palette and look above it (and hover any placed building with no block selected).

java: Java: select a block -> the pane above the category rail shows icon + localized name + block-select hotkey, a '?' button opening the content database, and one row per requirement with core-stock colouring; an unplaceable reason row appears when the block cannot be placed (PlacementFragment.java:344-438, 391-395, 399-428, 784-787).
Java: with no block selected, hovering a placed building shows its Displayable info in the same pane (PlacementFragment.java:433-436).
godot: Godot: select any block -> only the grid cell checks; there is no info pane in the fragment (its own header admits the box is pending, placement_fragment.gd:6-10) and the scene has only Search/Categories/Blocks (placement_fragment.tscn:19-45).

Hover a building -> nothing reads a hover/displayable model: client/rust/mind-core/src/ui/display.rs:48 (HoverInfo) has no consumer in mind-gdext/GDScript and no requirement, cost or '?' control is wired.
compare: Java always shows the selected block's name, requirements against core stock and a database '?' button; the port shows no block details at all, so players cannot see costs or open the block's info before placing.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: PlacementFragment has no top info table; the selected-block view model lives unused in client/rust/mind-core/src/ui/display.rs and needs a MindHud/MindUi JSON surface plus the scene cell.
plan.approach: 1) Expose a selected-block/hover info JSON (name bundle key, unlocked flag, requirements with amounts and current core counts via the existing core_items read model, unplaceable reason, hotkey) from MindHud/MindUi. 2) Add the Java-style top pane to placement_fragment.tscn above the category rail and populate it in placement_fragment.gd on selection/hover change (PlacementFragment.java:344-438): icon, label, '?' button calling MindUi.open_dialog('content', block), requirement rows coloured by core stock, and the unplaceable reason row. 3) Feed the hovered Displayable half from display.rs HoverInfo when the hover provider lands; the selected-block half is self-contained. 4) Narrow check: select a block and assert the pane shows its localized name and one requirement row, and that '?' opens the content dialog for it.
plan.narrow_check: In-engine: select a block, assert the info pane text/requirements; press '?' and assert the content dialog opens. Headless: a ui test covering the new info JSON for a block with requirements.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (hud-world-ui): S3 high confidence - the whole upper half of the placement fragment is missing, so block costs/unlock state and the database shortcut are invisible. PAR-0048 verifies only the category button + block grid; PAR-0065 covers the custom-game grid rows, not this pane. In-engine verification pending.

title: Holding Shift shows no command panel: the block palette stays and no unit/stance/command buttons appear

path.to: Live client with player-team units: hold Shift (command mode) and drag-select, then look at the bottom-right HUD.

java: Java: with command mode on, PlacementFragment swaps the block palette for commandTable (mainStack.update, PlacementFragment.java:446-455): a '@commandmode.name' header, selected unit stacks grouped by type, stance and command icon rows, and per-type select/remove (PlacementFragment.java:471-475, 500-560, 628-668).
godot: Godot: MindInput does toggle command mode on the Shift edge (desktop.rs:526-532; PAR-0063 verified the keyboard state), but no GDScript or scene references command mode at all (grep client/ui for command_mode/selectedUnits is empty); placement_fragment.gd only ever builds the category rail and block grid (lines 107-204, scene lines 19-45), so holding Shift leaves the block palette unchanged with no unit list, stance row or command buttons.
The selection event exists (MindInput.selection_changed, input/mod.rs:195) but nothing listens to it in the UI layer.
compare: Java replaces the palette with the command panel and drives mouse commands/stances from it; the port shows nothing new, so RTS commands are only reachable by hotkeys (and not at all until the selection feed lands).

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: placement_fragment.gd + its scene: Java's commandTable/mainStack swap has no port; unit rows come from the RTS selection surface (Input.selection_changed / selection_json).
plan.approach: 1) Add a command-panel node beside the block palette in placement_fragment.tscn. 2) Connect MindInput.selection_changed and the hotkey('command_mode') signal and swap palette <-> command panel exactly like Java's mainStack.update (PlacementFragment.java:446-455). 3) Render grouped unit-type rows from selection_json plus stance/command buttons that call the existing MindInput stub paths behind the unit_stance_* / unit_command_* bindings (desktop.rs:544-554); grey buttons the selected unit types do not allow. 4) Narrow check: in-engine hold Shift and assert the command panel is visible, and after a drag-select it lists the selected type (depends on the selection feed recorded in the units-ai 'RTS unit selection and orders do nothing' item).
plan.narrow_check: In-engine: hold Shift -> command panel visible; drag-select one unit -> its type row appears (requires the selection feed).

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (hud-world-ui): S3 high confidence - the command-mode HUD half is entirely absent, so command mode currently has no on-screen affordance. Shares the fix surface with the units-ai item 'RTS unit selection and orders do nothing: the selectable list is never fed and commands never reach live units' (that item covers selection/order behavior; this one covers the missing panel). In-engine verification pending.

title: Enemy attacks on your buildings never mark the minimap: no pulsing red attack indicators

path.to: Live client, any game mode: let an enemy damage a player-team building, then open the fullscreen minimap (or watch the HUD minimap).

java: Java: a BuildDamageEvent on a player-team building calls indicators.add(tile) (Control.java:68-71); Control ticks indicators.update() while playing (Control.java:711); MinimapRenderer draws pulsing orange->scarlet squares for each live indicator in fullscreen mode (MinimapRenderer.java:253-274).
godot: Godot: mind-core/src/game/attack_indicators.rs:33 exists but has no live caller (the only reference is mind-headless/src/campaign_scenarios.rs:646); nothing subscribes to BuildDamageEvent (defined at world/events.rs:125 but never emitted in mind-core) and neither render/minimap.rs nor ui/widgets/mind_minimap.gd (draw at :51-74) draws any indicator.
compare: Java shows where the base is being hit from on the minimap; the port never records or draws an indicator, so players have no minimap alert.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: No wiring from building damage to AttackIndicators (mind-core/src/game/attack_indicators.rs) and no minimap draw pass; the data must reach the minimap provider / MindMinimapWidget.
plan.approach: 1) Insert AttackIndicators as a sim/campaign resource and add the missing BuildDamageEvent emission when the live combat runtime damages a player-team building (mirror Control.java:68-71); tick AttackIndicators::update in the fixed step while playing (Control.java:711). 2) Expose attack_indicators_json() (packed pos + elapsed ticks) through the minimap provider (World/MinimapProvider) or MindHud. 3) Draw the pulsing squares in mind_minimap.gd (and the fullscreen fragment) using the Java geometry (radius = fin*5 + tilesize - 2, colour lerp orange->scarlet, MinimapRenderer.java:253-274), clipped to the minimap rect. 4) Narrow check: cargo test -p mind-core attack_indicators (add/expire) plus in-engine: damage a player building and assert an indicator row appears and draws.
plan.narrow_check: cargo test -p mind-core game::attack and an in-engine building-damage -> indicator pixel/row check.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (hud-world-ui): S3 high confidence for the dead display path - AttackIndicators is never fed and never drawn. Observation depends on enemy damage reaching player buildings (turret/enemy-AI gaps in the combat/units-ai scans), so the evaluator should force-damage a building or use a sandbox scenario. PAR-0032/0057 cover minimap rendering only; no ledger item covers indicators. In-engine verification pending.

title: F6 does nothing: no power/liquid/item status bars are drawn over buildings

path.to: Live client with placed consumer buildings (drill/turret/power node): press F6 and watch for status bars over the blocks.

java: Java: F6 toggles the 'blockstatus' setting (DesktopInput.java:455-457); Renderer.drawStatus reads it into the render flag (Renderer.java:170); BlockRenderer calls drawStatus() for every visible consumer building when enabled (BlockRenderer.java:825-833), which draws the power/liquid/item bars (BuildingComp.java:1221).
godot: Godot: pressing F6 fires the 'toggle_block_status' binding (binding.rs:763) into MindInput's dispatch_action, which has no arm for it (desktop.rs:481-600), so no setting or render flag changes.

Even with a flag forced, no status-bar pass exists: the render scan computes tile_with_consumer_view (mind-core/src/render/scan.rs:82) but no mind-gdext pass reads it, and render/blocks.rs:9 documents status bars as unlanded (M3/M4).
compare: Java's F6 reveals per-building power/liquid/item fill bars; the port's F6 is inert and no bar geometry is drawn.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: MindInput dispatch (client/rust/mind-gdext/src/input/desktop.rs:481) has no 'toggle_block_status' arm, and no render pass consumes tile_with_consumer_view (mind-core/src/render/scan.rs:82).
plan.approach: 1) Add a 'toggle_block_status' arm to dispatch_action that flips a persisted 'blockstatus' flag (default false, like Java's graphics.checkPref) and fire the hotkey signal. 2) Add a status-bar draw pass (new pass under Layer.overlay or extend overlays.rs) that consumes the scan's tile_with_consumer_view and draws each building's module ratios (PowerModule.status, LiquidModule.current/capacity, ItemModule.total/capacity) as the Java bar strips (Building.drawStatus -> BuildingComp.java:1221). 3) Gate the pass on the flag and Lod level 2 like Java. 4) Narrow check: in-engine place a fed consumer, press F6, assert bar quads appear (RenderStats counter) and pressing again removes them; headless: assert the flag round-trips through MindInput.
plan.narrow_check: In-engine F6 toggle with a consumer building visible: bar draw count > 0 on enable, 0 on disable.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (hud-world-ui): S3 high confidence - the concrete F6 control is dead and the in-world block status readout (power/liquid/items) never renders; core-items HUD (CoreItemsDisplay) and wave pane do work, so this is the missing per-building status half of lead 8. Bars default off in Java, so the repro must enable F6. In-engine verification pending.
